ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: The image shows a transition-state structure with a benzene ring on the left fused/attached to a right-hand cyclic carbonyl-containing portion. At the top right there is a carbonyl group C=O, and to its right is an upper NH connected downward to another NH. The lower part contains a central carbon connected to the fused lower ring carbon, to an O− group, and to an exocyclic NH that is further connected to R. Curved arrows are present near the lower atoms, but the question says to disregard arrows. Reasoning/count: Count heavy-atom bonds only, excluding all bonds to hydrogen. The benzene ring contributes 6 heavy-atom bonds around the ring. The right-hand/carbonyl-containing portion contributes 6 more: fused top carbon–carbonyl carbon, carbonyl C=O, carbonyl carbon–upper NH, upper NH–lower NH, lower NH–central carbon, and central carbon–lower fused carbon. The lower substituent part contributes 3 more: central carbon–O−, central carbon–exocyclic NH, and exocyclic NH–R. Total = 6 + 6 + 3 = 15.

method.method_draft: First describe the image as a heavy-atom graph, then compute degrees. The six benzene carbons contribute degrees 14 in total: two fused carbons each have three heavy-atom neighbors and the other four benzene carbons each have two. The remaining vertices contribute: carbonyl carbon 3, carbonyl oxygen 1, upper NH 2, lower NH 2, central carbon 4, O− 1, exocyclic NH 2, and R attachment 1. The heavy-atom degree sum is 14 + 3 + 1 + 2 + 2 + 4 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 30, so the number of bonds is 30/2 = 15.
